lead.tldr: DeFi United fund shows community willingness to self‑insure, but governance risk remains for Kelp DAO remediation • Israel's shekel‑pegged stablecoin BILS introduces non‑USD exposure, opening regulatory‑compliant on‑ramp for Middle East investors • AML enforcement surge eclipses SEC actions, indicating compliance costs will dominate crypto operating budgets in 2026 • Bitmine's $294 m Ether accumulation signals confidence in US legislative outcome and potential supply pressure on ETH market • Bitcoin dip below $76k tied to oil price shock and risk‑off sentiment may suppress crypto rally until tensions ease • Solana's Falcon post‑quantum test demonstrates proactive security hardening, potentially attracting institutional validators seeking future‑proof infrastructure

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, DeFi United has mobilised $300 million to repair the Kelp DAO breach and Israel unveiled its first regulated shekel‑pegged stablecoin. Meanwhile, AML fines are soaring as regulators tighten crypto oversight.

top_signals.title: Aave-led 'DeFi United' campaign raises $300m to address Kelp DAO breach
top_signals.summary: Aave is leading the DeFi United campaign that has secured more than $300 million to compensate victims of the Kelp DAO/LayerZero breach that resulted in a $293 million loss. The recovery fund is being populated by contributions of Ether and stablecoins from a range of major DAOs, crypto enterprises and prominent individuals, reflecting broad sector support. This coordinated response underscores the growing capacity of decentralized‑finance participants to mobilize capital for risk mitigation and reinforces confidence among institutional investors in the ecosystem’s resilience.

top_signals.title: A digital shekel is here: Israel approves its first-ever regulated stablecoin
top_signals.summary: Israel's Capital Market Authority has approved BILS, the country's first regulated stablecoin that is pegged to the Israeli shekel. The token is issued by Bits of Gold in partnership with the Solana blockchain, with custody services provided by Fireblocks and audit oversight from EY. This approval introduces a locally denominated digital asset and diversifies the stablecoin market beyond the dominant USD‑pegged offerings, which may be of interest to institutional investors seeking exposure to Israeli currency and regulated crypto infrastructure.

top_signals.title: Aave publishes plan to plug $246m hole left by Kelp DAO attackers
top_signals.summary: Aave has released a detailed plan to address the $246 million shortfall created by the Kelp DAO attack. The plan is coordinated with Compound and the DeFi United coalition to fully back rsETH and eliminate the bad debt. It calls for converting pledged ETH into rsETH and using governance votes to lower oracle prices so that controlled liquidations can be executed. Successful implementation would return the stolen assets to the users affected by the hack and restore confidence in the protocol’s risk management.

top_signals.title: AML Fines Eclipse SEC Cases as Top Crypto Risk: Report
top_signals.summary: A new report shows that anti‑money‑laundering penalties for crypto firms have risen sharply, with sanctions‑related volume increasing more than 400 percent year over year. The report notes that these AML fines now outweigh the number of SEC enforcement actions, positioning regulatory risk as the top concern for the sector. This enforcement trend is occurring alongside tighter stablecoin regulations being applied by regulators. At the same time, the Basel Committee is preparing prudential standards that would require near‑full capital charges on major crypto assets such as Bitcoin and Ether, adding further capital cost considerations for institutional investors.

top_signals.title: Bitmine buys $294m more Ethereum ahead of Clarity Act ‘markup in May’
top_signals.summary: Bitmine increased its Ether position by $294 million, raising its total exposure to about $12 billion, which represents roughly 4.2 % of the total Ether supply. The timing aligns with the U.S. Senate’s upcoming markup of the Clarity Act, a legislative step aimed at establishing a federal digital‑asset framework. The transaction is supported by a consortium of prominent investors including ARK, Founders Fund, Pantera, Kraken, Galaxy Digital and Bill Miller, underscoring institutional confidence in the asset ahead of potential regulatory clarity.

top_signals.title: Bitcoin Faces Fresh Oil Woes With a BTC Price Dip Under $76,000
top_signals.summary: Bitcoin slipped below $76,000, marking a one week low. The decline coincided with oil prices breaking $100 per barrel as concerns over a renewed blockade of the Strait of Hormuz intensified. Heightened United States Iran geopolitical tension reduced risk appetite in both cryptocurrency and equity markets, underscoring the sensitivity of digital assets to macro geopolitical shocks.

top_signals.title: Galaxy Posts $216M Q1 Loss as Helios Expansion Advances
top_signals.summary: Galaxy Digital disclosed a first‑quarter loss of $216 million and a full‑year net loss of $241 million, attributing the decline to weaker digital‑asset prices. The firm emphasized progress on its Helios data‑center campus in Texas, which is being built to support AI‑linked infrastructure. Helios is expected to begin generating revenue in Q2 2026, providing a potential new income stream as the company diversifies beyond market‑price exposure.

top_signals.title: Japan Requests Real Estate and Crypto Firms Tighten AML Checks on Property Deals
top_signals.summary: Japan’s Financial Services Agency has instructed real‑estate agents and cryptocurrency firms to apply bank‑style anti‑money‑laundering (AML) checks to property transactions that involve crypto assets. The guidance classifies the conversion of crypto to fiat currency as a regulated exchange activity and requires reporting of large foreign crypto inflows that exceed set thresholds. The move aims to tighten oversight of cross‑border crypto flows in the real‑estate market, a development that institutional investors should monitor as it may affect compliance costs and transaction structuring.

top_signals.title: Canaan Lands New Tether Order as Mining Shifts to Modular Infrastructure
top_signals.summary: Canaan has received a new order from Tether for Bitcoin mining hardware. Tether is shifting its mining operations to a modular infrastructure model. The deal underscores rising demand for mining capacity that is financed or backed by stablecoins. It also signals institutional confidence in Canaan’s modular hardware solutions as a scalable approach for the industry.

top_signals.title: Bitcoin mining meltdown? Why IREN’s real future is in AI, according to Bernstein
top_signals.summary: IREN, previously known for Bitcoin mining, is redirecting its primary operations toward AI cloud infrastructure. The company projects that the new focus will generate multi‑billion‑dollar revenues and high EBITDA margins by 2030. Bernstein has kept an outperform rating on IREN, viewing the strategic shift as a key growth catalyst. The analyst firm also lowered its price target, reflecting a more conservative valuation despite the positive outlook.

top_signals.title: Solana Clients Introduce Post-Quantum Solution Falcon
top_signals.summary: Solana validator clients Anza and Firedancer have released test implementations of the Falcon post‑quantum signature scheme to prepare the network for future quantum threats. Falcon‑512 is the smallest NIST‑approved post‑quantum signature and can be verified off‑chain, which helps preserve Solana’s high‑throughput performance. The integration demonstrates proactive security hardening in the Solana ecosystem and may be of interest to institutional investors monitoring blockchain resilience.

linkedin_post: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, The past weeks have shown how quickly the DeFi ecosystem can rally around a crisis and how regulators are paving new pathways for digital assets. Aave has taken the lead in the DeFi United campaign, gathering more than $300 million from DAOs, crypto enterprises and individual contributors to compensate victims of the Kelp DAO and LayerZero breach. This coordinated fund demonstrates that decentralized finance participants can mobilise capital at scale and gives institutional investors a clear signal of growing risk‑mitigation capacity. At the same time, Israel’s Capital Market Authority has approved BILS, the country’s first regulated stablecoin pegged to the shekel. Issued by Bits of Gold on Solana, with custody by Fireblocks and audit oversight from EY, the token adds a locally denominated digital asset to the market. For investors looking for exposure beyond the USD‑pegged stablecoin universe, the digital shekel opens a fresh avenue backed by a robust regulatory framework. Aave has also published a detailed plan to close the $246 million shortfall left by the Kelp attackers. Working with Compound and the DeFi United coalition, the proposal converts pledged ETH into rsETH, adjusts oracle prices through governance votes and executes controlled liquidations. If successful, the plan will restore assets to affected users and reinforce confidence in protocol risk management.
